integratedBehavior: Windows credentials and project database/object keys are distinct, current-user DPAPI-protected records under one verified profile-vault authority. Callers supply a closed capability, purpose and scope and receive short-lived zeroed leases; secret values and identifying scope do not enter project databases, exports, support bundles, command lines, environment dumps, or default audit output.

The native desktop supervisor owns application lock. Manual, inactivity, startup/reconciliation failure and restart paths invalidate protected generations, cancel Core work, clear previews and renderer project state, and render only the accessible locked surface. Unlock uses a non-persisting Windows prompt, validates the same Windows SID with bounded backoff, zeroes transient credential buffers, and starts a fresh Core capability without claiming account isolation.

Project privacy defaults to offline provider policy and telemetry off. Non-offline egress requires the exact project, provider mode, disclosure revision and informed acknowledgement; append-only revisions survive restart. Cache deletion requires a one-time preview and stable Windows identities, excludes canonical state, denies redirects and late namespace insertion, publishes a redacted audit, and distinguishes logical removal, best-effort cleanup and cryptographic erasure honestly.

Production project creation/open composes SQLCipher 4.12 before the first SQL operation using a random per-project raw 256-bit database key from the profile vault. Writable plaintext opens fail closed outside the explicit test fixture. Migration requires consent and publishes only the verified encrypted copy; backup/restore and rekey retain a recoverable prior authority until the new encrypted database passes integrity and restart verification.

The strict credential-store, application-lock, privacy-policy and protected-database contracts expose portable versions and policy outcomes without Windows paths, secret bytes, SQLite connections, renderer state, or provider-specific DTOs. CAP-02 storage and future capabilities consume those ports rather than private adapter state.
